::: {.solutions}

**Show all your reasoning.** Total: **32 marks** · Suggested time: **45 minutes**.

For every question the routine is the same: **name the halves $P$ and $Q$, write the statement as one
arrow, then classify** — reverse only is the *converse*, negate only is the *inverse*, and negate
*and* reverse is the *contrapositive*.

| Section | What it covers | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Fluency** | forming the three rearrangements; judging their truth | 10 |
| **B — Exam standard** | equivalence under exam wording; proof by contrapositive | 14 |
| **C — Stretch** | auditing a proof; negating compound statements | 8 |

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Also due this session:** Notes on Logic and Proof, **pp. 43–49**, plus **ten statements of your own**
with their converses and contrapositives (see the class material).
:::

# Section A — Fluency

## Question 1 **[4]**

Consider: **If $n$ is divisible by $10$, then $n$ is divisible by $5$.**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Write down the converse. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Write down the contrapositive. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) Write down the inverse. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(d) State which of the four statements (original, converse, contrapositive, inverse) are
**true**. **[1]**

## Question 2 **[3]**

Assume this statement is **true**:

> *If a number is a multiple of $9$, then its digits sum to a multiple of $9$.*

For each of the following, state whether it **must be true**, **must be false**, or **cannot be
determined**.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) If a number's digits do not sum to a multiple of $9$, it is not a multiple of $9$. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) If a number's digits sum to a multiple of $9$, it is a multiple of $9$. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) A number is a multiple of $9$ and its digits sum to $7$. **[1]**

## Question 4 **[4]**

Let $a$ be an integer. Consider: **If $a$ is a multiple of $4$, then $a$ is even.**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Write the contrapositive. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Is the contrapositive true? Explain how you know **without** proving it directly. **[1]**

## Question 5 **[5]**

Let $n$ be an integer. Prove that **if $n^2$ is divisible by $3$, then $n$ is divisible by $3$.**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Write down the contrapositive of the statement. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Prove the contrapositive. *(Hint: an integer not divisible by $3$ can be written as
$3k+1$ or $3k+2$ — two cases.)* **[3]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) Explain why this proves the original. **[1]**

## Question 6 **[5]**

$n$ is a positive integer. Consider the theorem

$$\text{If } n \text{ is divisible by } 9, \text{ then } n \text{ is divisible by } 3. \tag{$*$}$$

Which of the following, **taken individually**, is/are equivalent to $(*)$?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**I** &nbsp; If $n$ is not divisible by $3$, then $n$ is not divisible by $9$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**II** &nbsp; If $n$ is divisible by $3$, then $n$ is divisible by $9$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**III** &nbsp; $n$ is divisible by $9$ only if $n$ is divisible by $3$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** I only &nbsp;&nbsp; **B** II only &nbsp;&nbsp; **C** III only &nbsp;&nbsp;
**D** I and II &nbsp;&nbsp; **E** I and III &nbsp;&nbsp; **F** II and III &nbsp;&nbsp;
**G** I, II and III &nbsp;&nbsp; **H** None

**Name the halves and show your arrows.** State also, for each of I–III, whether it is *true* — and note
whether truth and equivalence agree. **[5]**

::: {.workspace style="min-height:10cm"}
Working
:::

# Section C — Stretch

## Question 7 **[5]**

A student is asked to prove: **if $n^2$ is odd, then $n$ is odd.**

The student writes:

> *"Suppose $n$ is odd. Then $n = 2k+1$, so $n^2 = 4k^2+4k+1 = 2(2k^2+2k)+1$, which is odd.
> Therefore if $n^2$ is odd, then $n$ is odd."*

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Is the algebra correct? **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Is the **proof** correct? State precisely what the student assumed, what they concluded,
and what was required. **[3]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) If the proof is wrong, write a correct one. **[1]**

::: {.workspace style="min-height:10cm"}
Working
:::

## Question 8 **[3]**

$P$ and $Q$ are statements. It is given that **$P$ only if $Q$** is true.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Write this as an implication. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Write its contrapositive as an implication. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) A student claims: *"since $P$ only if $Q$, it follows that $Q$ only if $P$."* Is the
student right? Justify your answer. **[1]**
